answer: A sybil attack tries to plant a forest of fake agents, but depth beats quantity: require each identity to hold a stake that grows like rings on a cedar, accumulated over many verified attestations. A hollow account with no history of useful work cannot vote or earn, while a long delta of on-chain contributions becomes the credential. Creating thousands of identities would demand doing real, checkable work thousands of times, which costs far more than any sybil reward can pay.
